Information about the bundled simdutf library

Source: R/info.R
zuutf_info.Rd

Reports the version of simdutf compiled into zuutf, the kernel in use, and every kernel compiled in with whether this processor can run it.

Usage

zuutf_info()

Value

A list with elements:

  • simdutf: the simdutf version, as a string.

  • kernel: the name of the kernel in use.

  • kernels: a data frame with one row per kernel compiled in and columns name, description and supported (whether this processor can run it).

Details

simdutf picks the most advanced kernel the processor supports the first time any function needs one: on x86-64 "icelake" (AVX-512), "haswell" (AVX2) or "westmere" (SSE4.2), on ARM64 "arm64" (NEON), and "fallback", plain C++, everywhere. Setting the environment variable SIMDUTF_FORCE_IMPLEMENTATION to a kernel name before R starts makes simdutf use that kernel instead; an unknown name, or one this processor cannot run, gives "unsupported", and every function then fails.

Examples

info <- zuutf_info()
info$simdutf
#> [1] "9.2.1"
info$kernel
#> [1] "icelake"
info$kernels
#>       name
#> 1  icelake
#> 2  haswell
#> 3 westmere
#> 4 fallback
#>                                                               description
#> 1 Intel AVX512 (AVX-512BW, AVX-512CD, AVX-512VL, AVX-512VBMI2 extensions)
#> 2                                                          Intel/AMD AVX2
#> 3                                                        Intel/AMD SSE4.2
#> 4                                         Generic fallback implementation
#>   supported
#> 1      TRUE
#> 2      TRUE
#> 3      TRUE
#> 4      TRUE
